e: Probably borrowed from German uzen (“to kid; tease”).
q: He picked up several large canteloupes, hefted them for weight, then utzed the farmer, “Hey, can't you sabras grow bigger peaches than these?”
1992, Leo Rosten, The Joys of Yinglish:
The girl with the auburn hair was lingering, too. Her name was Susan. She was talking with the blonde who had utzed her to talk to Vonnegut.
